newsitem.title: BELGIUM: BELGIAN SHARES SET FOR FURTHER GAINS BUT FRAGILE.
newsitem.headline: BELGIAN SHARES SET FOR FURTHER GAINS BUT FRAGILE.

text.p: Wall Street continued to dictate the trend for the Bel-20 index, which closed at a record high for the second day in a row on Wednesday, but dealers warned that the market remained vulnerable.
"The market is going up, up, up but it's still vulnerable. Let's wait for Friday's (U.S.) data," one trader said.
U.S. September unemployment and payrolls data are due at 1230 GMT on Friday.
The Bel-20, also lifted by strong bonds but practically ignoring the Belgian 1997 budget presented on Tuesday, closed at a record 1,790.52 points, up 11.36 points or 0.64 percent.
The index earlier set an intra-day record high at 1,792.59.
Dealers said foreign institutionals were giving the budget a positive reading.
"The budget has no negative impact, the government has been remarkably consistent (in drafting its budget)," one said.
The Belgian government said Tuesday its 1997 budget would propel it into Europe's economic and monetary union in 1999.

The budget should cut the total public sector deficit to 2.9 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), from an estimated 3.3 percent in 1996 through an austerity package worth 80 billion Belgian francs ($2.5 billion).
The retail sector was the flavour of the day with dollar-sensitive Delhaize up 2.0 percent at 1,815 after earlier setting a record at 1,840. Colruyt surged 4.1 percent to 13,300.
But one dealer said Colruyt and Delhaize had become expensive in price/earnings terms and advised a hold on both.
GIB, due to publish H1 1996 earnings on Thursday, added 0.2 percent to 1,304 even though analysts predicted losses at its Quick fast-food chain unit would dampen GIB's profit rise.
Quick surged 4.3 percent to 2,450 but dealers said it was merely a technical rebound in an empty market. The share was still at 2,780 francs late August.
One dealer said banking stocks had been strong on Wall Street on Wednesday and would take over the relay baton from retailers in Brussels on Thursday.
Leading holding Generale de Belgique ended unchanged at 2,465 after reporting Tuesday that first-half 1996 group net profit rose six percent to 6.72 billion Belgian francs.
